messages.subject: rApache powered websites
parts:
Hi there,
can anybody share a working example of a rApache driven website
(beyond Jeroen's examples)?
I am working on a webpage myself but I am curious about any use cases.
Best, Maciej

messages.author: 30b7291c5e29905a
messages.subject: Re: rApache powered websites
parts:
I have a beta version of an rApache driven ETF rotational investment strategy site at :  http://kwantboxx.com/aux/test.html

Be gentle...this is on my home server....

Just enter an integer in each field , click submit, and give it a minute to calculate the data, graphs, etc. (ex. enter '3' for each field)

The one thing I am unsure how to do is to get an accurate progress meter...currently I guesstimate the length of time it takes to produce the charts and randomly increment the progress bar over the time I *think* it should take.  Any other suggestions are certainly welcome.

Dennis

Nice, I like it.
Unfortunately, I cannot help you with the progress bar so far,
But, is the run time roughly the same for any realistic data range?

Moreover, you will need the numeric field validators etc.
Also, the 'submit' button is active even with no data at all and
can be fired with no values at all.

Are you using brew or calling R with the 'sys.source'?
M

messages.subject: Re: rApache powered websites
parts:
I'm using brew.

My "front-end" code...the wrapper with the form and submit button calls /var/www/brew/xxxx.R
From within the R code, I use Cairo to produce the graphs and display them in a separate frame.

I found the example code of UseR2007! very helpful in getting things up and going.
